name: E-9 Non-Professional Employment (Employment Permit System, EPS)

requirements.blocker_text: Only available to nationals of countries with a signed EPS bilateral MOU with Korea (17 countries as of this research, including Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines, Indonesia, and India, added as the 17th partner in late 2023) -- recruitment runs government-to-government through each country's official sending agency, and private brokers cannot legally charge placement fees.

Requires passing the EPS-TOPIK test (40 multiple-choice questions on workplace Korean, scored out of 100) and being ranked into the Worker Roster; selection is by relative ranking against the country-and-sector quota, not a fixed pass score, so passing does not guarantee placement.
requirements.fix_path: Retake the EPS-TOPIK to improve ranking within the quota competition.

requirements.blocker_text: Limited to five designated low-to-mid-skilled sectors: manufacturing, agriculture and livestock, fisheries, construction, and a small service-sector allocation.

evidence_required.document: EPS-TOPIK test result and Worker Roster ranking
Health check meeting EPS medical standards
Employer's approved quota allocation and employment permit

outcome.duration_length: up to 4 years and 10 months maximum
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: workplace changes restricted to specific circumstances (business closure, contract violation, injury, contract end); unauthorised changes can void the status

sources.title: Korea.net (Korean Culture and Information Service, Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism) -- 'Non-professional foreign worker quota for 2026 set at 191K', 23 Dec 2025, reporting the Foreign Workforce Policy Committee's decision

notes: LIVE DISCREPANCY, directly caught via a tier-1 fetch: the official 2026 E-9 quota, set by the Foreign Workforce Policy Committee on 22 Dec 2025 and reported on korea.net, is 80,000 (split 50,000 manufacturing / 10,000 agriculture-livestock / 7,000 fisheries / 2,000 construction / 1,000 service, plus 10,000 flexible reserve), alongside a separate 109,000 E-8 seasonal-worker quota, for a combined 191,000 non-professional-worker ceiling. Secondary sources checked in this research pass report wildly different, mutually inconsistent figures for the same year -- one cites 165,000 E-9 + 53,000 E-8; another cites a flat '33,000 spots' with no sector breakdown; a third describes an '80,000' figure that matches the tier-1 source only by coincidence, since it's presented without corroborating detail. The tier-1 korea.net figure (80,000 E-9 / 109,000 E-8 / 191,000 combined, with the specific sector breakdown) is treated as authoritative here precisely because it's the only account with underlying committee-level administrative detail rather than a bare headline number -- a clear example of why this dataset prioritises direct government-source fetches over search-retrieved secondary figures, even when several secondary sources cluster around a different number. selection_odds is left null rather than estimated: EPS selection is a relative ranking against per-country-per-sector sub-quotas, not a single national lottery or a published pass/placement rate, and no tier-1 source in this research pass gave a defensible single probability figure -- an invented approximation would misrepresent the mechanism more than it would inform an applicant, so this is an honest gap rather than a guess. E-9 holders cannot bring family (family_can_join: false) -- one of the starkest work-rights restrictions in this entire dataset given the route's scale (tens of thousands of workers annually). The standard long-term path out is conversion to E-7-4 (Skilled Worker Points system) after 4+ years on E-9 within the past 10 years, at least 1 year with the current registered employer, salary ≥KRW 26 million (KRW 25 million for agriculture/fisheries), an employer recommendation, and 200+/300 on the K-Point assessment -- not modeled as a separate requirement_group on kr_e7_designated_activities in this initial build (see that route's notes for the flagged expansion candidate) but captured here via switchable_to.
